title: 离自动驾驶又近一步！特斯拉FSD V14发布 马斯克：产生意识了
content: Tesla has released FSD V14, marking a major step toward full self-driving, with Elon Musk claiming the system now 'feels alive' and exhibits signs of consciousness. The update introduces a unified architecture between量产 vehicles and Tesla Robotaxi, powered by a neural network with at least hundreds of billions to trillions of parameters—4.5 to 10 times larger than V13. Key improvements include full 'door-to-door' autonomous driving, handling of complex private roads (e.g., unstructured driveways and cluttered garages), precise recognition of drive-thru payment and pickup zones (e.g., McDonald's), dynamic parking spot acquisition in busy lots, and real-time response to emergency vehicles. The system now autonomously adjusts behavior—such as reversing at a red light or yielding to fire trucks—demonstrating advanced situational awareness. It also features new functions: Arrival Options (customizable parking types), emergency vehicle detection, real-time rerouting for roadblocks, customizable 'speed modes' including a conservative 'SLOTH' mode, enhanced obstacle avoidance, system stability during failures, and an automatic windshield cleaning system. Despite official disclaimers requiring human supervision, the functional maturity of FSD V14 now closely mirrors Robotaxi-level capabilities. This represents the first true convergence of production vehicles and Robotaxi under a single architecture. The update is only available on HW4.0 hardware, highlighting Tesla’s ability to optimize massive models within constrained compute (hundreds of TOPS). This achievement challenges industry norms, as most competitors require over 2000 TOPS for similar model scales. Musk’s claim that FSD now 'feels alive' reflects a shift toward large-vision-language model (VLA)-based perception. The update signals a pivotal moment in the evolution of autonomous driving: the blurring of the line between L2 and L4, the bypassing of geographic licensing barriers, and the potential for rapid, universal deployment. The broader automotive industry may now face a new competitive divide—determined not by sensor count or raw compute, but by full-stack, hardware-software integration. The stage is set for a convergence of technology, business models, and market structure in 2025.

title: 汽车行业双周报：特斯拉FSD V14发布在即，智驾范式...
content: Tesla’s Full Self‑Driving (FSD) version 14 is slated to launch next week, followed by 14.1 two weeks later and 14.2 as the final release. Elon Musk announced on X that the new version will bring the vehicle to a level of perception that feels 'almost like a sentient life form'. The update is expected to feature a model with roughly ten times the number of parameters of previous releases and to incorporate near‑real‑time network and audio data, giving the system multimodal perception that moves from a geometric‑to‑physical‑world understanding. According to the overseas teslafsdtracker site, since the release of FSD12 the average takeover mileage per incident rose from about 100 miles to roughly 200 miles with FSD13, while high‑speed takeover mileage jumped from 20‑30 miles on FSD10.x to over 200 miles on FSD13.x, indicating a highly efficient iteration cycle. Analysts say the parameter growth could produce a non‑linear 'intelligence emergence' and that Tesla’s data advantage may shift from sheer volume to volume + quality, deepening competitive barriers. The article recommends monitoring domestic Chinese EV makers such as Xpeng and Li Auto, upstream component suppliers like Black Sesame Intelligent and Horizon Robotics, and robotaxi firms such as Xiaoma Zhixing, Wen Yuan Zhi Xing, Qianli Technology, and Yong'an Xing. Risks highlighted include delayed rollout, under‑performance, and technical path uncertainty.

title: Tesla FSD (Supervised) Rolls-Out to Owners in Australia and New Zealand | Man of Many
content: Tesla’s Full Self‑Driving (Supervised) has been rolled out to owners in Australia and New Zealand via an over‑the‑air update. The feature is only available to vehicles equipped with Hardware 4, specifically the Model 3 and Model Y, meaning older‑generation cars are excluded. Customers who already own FSD can update their cars on Thursday, 18 September 2025, while new buyers can purchase the full FSD Capability for AUD 10,100. Tesla also plans a subscription model: AUD 150 per month (NZD 159) or AUD 1,800 per year, which would take nearly six years to break even compared with a one‑time purchase, though used‑car prices may rise faster. Test‑drive vehicles will be available at Tesla Stores in Australia and New Zealand from the same date, with a 30‑day free trial still unconfirmed. Tesla’s release notes explain safety protocols: if the cabin camera cannot see the driver’s hand or arm, the touchscreen warns the driver; repeated distraction triggers a warning sound, and ignoring further warnings disables FSD (Supervised) and may bring the car to a stop with hazard lights. After five suspensions the driver’s access is revoked. The author, who tested the system on Brisbane roads, described it as “the best advanced driver assistance system I’ve ever used (by a long margin)” but emphasized that the vehicle is not autonomous and a human must remain in control. The rollout is described as a significant step for transport in the region, with Australia and New Zealand being the first right‑hand‑drive markets to receive the technology.

title: Tesla's 'Full Self-Driving' software under investigation for traffic safety violations | TechCrunch
content: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has opened a Preliminary Evaluation into Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software following reports of safety violations, including vehicles running red lights, crossing into opposing lanes, and turning the wrong way despite clear signage. The investigation, launched on October 9, 2025, identified at least 18 complaints, two media reports, and six reports under the Standing General Order for Crash Reporting (SGO) from Tesla, involving 18 incidents where FSD failed to stop at red lights or remained stopped improperly. Additionally, six incidents involved FSD entering opposing lanes during or after turns, crossing double-yellow lines, or attempting wrong-way turns. Some incidents involved sudden, unannounced lane changes with little driver warning. The NHTSA noted multiple repeat incidents at the same intersection in Joppa, Maryland, where Tesla has already taken corrective action. The probe is one of the first specific to FSD, following a prior investigation into Tesla's Autopilot system that led to 13 fatal crashes linked to misuse and remains open for evaluation of Tesla’s fix. The new FSD investigation began the same week Tesla released an updated version of the software, incorporating data from its limited robotaxi pilot in Austin, Texas. Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency reportedly reduced NHTSA’s vehicle automation safety staff earlier in 2025, raising concerns about oversight capacity. The NHTSA typically completes such evaluations within eight months, though the federal government shutdown may affect the timeline.

title: 特斯拉FSD，近一年来首次重大更新
content: Tesla has rolled out its first major update to Full Self-Driving (FSD) in nearly a year, releasing the initial version of FSD V14.1 to U.S. users on October 6, 2025, starting with vehicles equipped with HW4.0 hardware. The update, originally scheduled for September 2025 but delayed due to a 'system vulnerability,' integrates technology from Tesla's Robotaxi autonomous taxi project. Key improvements in FSD V14.1 include: 1) Arrival Options allowing drivers to select parking spots (parking lot, street, private driveway, garage, curb); 2) Emergency vehicle detection and yielding; 3) Integration of navigation and path planning into the visual neural network for real-time handling of road blockages; 4) Additional speed profiles for personalized driving styles; 5) Optimized logic for static and dynamic barriers; 6) Enhanced obstacle avoidance (tires, branches, boxes); 7) Improved handling of unprotected turns, lane changes, vehicle cut-ins, and school bus scenarios; 8) Better system fault management with smooth recovery; 9) Automatic narrow-field windshield cleaning with optimized aerodynamics at high speeds; and 10) Internal residue warning on the windshield. Tesla plans further improvements in driving smoothness, parking precision, arrival options, and parking quality. However, China lags behind: as of February 25, 2025, Tesla only released FSD V2024.45.32.12 in China, limited to urban Autopilot enhancements, while the U.S. had already deployed FSD V13 with 'point-to-point' capabilities. Tesla CEO Elon Musk cited challenges such as complex bus lanes and regulatory and technical constraints in China. An industry expert testing FSD V13.2.9 reported that Tesla’s system outperformed other vision-based domestic automakers and was the only one to pass China’s new mandatory highway test involving a 50-cm cardboard box.

title: 特斯拉推出最新"完全自动驾驶"系统 | 完全自动驾驶系统 | 最新版本 | FSD v14 | 大纪元
content: Tesla announced on Tuesday, October 7, 2025, the launch of its latest 'Full Self-Driving' (FSD) system version, FSD v14.1, marking the most significant update to its autonomous driving technology in over a year. The new version is a supervised FSD system, though CEO Elon Musk had previously indicated plans for an unsupervised FSD version called 'FSD Unsupervised.' Tesla released two teaser videos over the weekend—featuring a rotating Tesla emblem and a dark silhouette of a car headlight—ending with the text '10/7,' signaling the product reveal. The teasers generated widespread online discussion and contributed to a 5% rise in Tesla’s stock price on Monday. The FSD v14.1 system may be integrated into a long-awaited low-cost model, a new Roadster, or another vehicle. Since 2016, Musk has repeatedly promised a fully autonomous vehicle capable of transporting passengers without human intervention. He also pledged to convert existing Tesla vehicles into robotaxis via software updates. In late June 2025, Tesla began limited deployment of autonomous robotaxis in Austin, Texas, with only about ten vehicles initially operating under strict conditions, including the presence of a safety operator in the front passenger seat. According to Tesla, FSD v14.1 represents a major advancement in autonomous driving. While human supervision is still required, the update enhances real-time navigation, smoother handling, and improved responsiveness to dynamic road conditions. Notably, the system can now dynamically reroute around blocked roads and more quickly identify emergency vehicles such as police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances, safely yielding when they approach. These improvements are reported by Teslarati and underscore progress toward fully autonomous driving.

title: 特斯拉V14发布：Robotaxi成果被整合！马斯克：FSD产生意识了
content: Tesla has officially rolled out the FSD V14 update, marking a major milestone in autonomous driving technology. The update features a neural network with at least hundreds of billions or even trillions of parameters—estimated to be 4.5 to 10 times larger than V13—enabling full end-to-end visual navigation and true architectural parity between量产 vehicles and Tesla's Robotaxi. Key improvements include door-to-door autonomous driving (including parking, toll payment, and navigating irregular private roads without prior map data), dynamic obstacle avoidance, real-time handling of road closures, emergency vehicle detection (e.g., fire trucks), and the new 'SLOTH' driving mode for conservative behavior. The system now autonomously identifies payment zones at drive-thrus (e.g., McDonald's), secures parking spots upon vacancy, and reacts to traffic signals and emergency vehicles with human-like judgment—such as backing up when a light turns red or yielding immediately to emergency vehicles. Elon Musk claimed the system 'feels alive' and 'has developed consciousness.' While official documentation still requires human supervision, the functionality closely mirrors that of Tesla’s Robotaxi, indicating the first real-world deployment of a unified architecture across L2 and L4 systems. Only vehicles equipped with HW4.0 hardware can run V14, showcasing Tesla’s ability to optimize massive models under constrained compute (hundreds of TOPS). This breakthrough suggests that future distinctions between 'autonomous' and 'assisted' driving may no longer hinge on sensor count or raw compute, but on full-stack, hardware-software integration. The update signals a pivotal shift in the industry toward large model-based, general-purpose autonomy, potentially ending the era of fragmented, supplier-dependent 'self-developed' systems. The article speculates that 2025 may mark a convergence point in autonomous driving technology, business models, and competitive dynamics. The update was published on October 9, 2025, via k.sina.com.cn.

content: Tesla has released its first major update to Full Self-Driving (FSD) in nearly a year, rolling out the initial version of FSD V14.1 to U.S. users on Monday night, local time, following the earlier rollout of V13 in December 2024. title: 特斯拉FSD v14发布：整合Robotaxi技术，新增多项驾驶与安全功能
content: Tesla has begun rolling out the first version of FSD v14.1 to users in North America, marking the first major update to the Full Self-Driving (FSD) system in nearly a year. The update integrates technological advancements from Tesla's Robotaxi autonomous taxi project. Despite CEO Elon Musk's repeated claims that FSD would soon achieve 'driverless autonomy,' Tesla has not yet fulfilled this promise. The development team had focused on the Austin Robotaxi project for several months, and FSD v14 incorporates some of its research findings into the consumer version. Originally scheduled for release in September, the rollout was delayed by one day due to the discovery of a 'bug.' Early adopters with HW4 hardware have reported that FSD v14's automated parking performance exceeds expectations, even surpassing that of human drivers. Key improvements include enhanced navigation, environmental perception, and user controls. Users can now initiate FSD Supervised mode via the central touchscreen or the right scroll wheel on the steering wheel and adjust 'speed levels' and 'arrival options' in real time. Tesla emphasizes that FSD (Supervised) still requires driver attention and control. The system can handle automatic start, lane changes, route branching, obstacle avoidance, turning, and automated parking, but does not grant full autonomous capability. The 'Brake Confirm' feature is disabled by default and can be manually re-enabled in 'Autopilot Settings.' Tesla plans to further improve driving smoothness, parking precision, arrival position options, and parking quality in future updates. The release of FSD v14 is considered the most significant system-wide upgrade to Tesla's autonomous driving technology in the past year and signals the company's shift toward applying Robotaxi project innovations to mass-market vehicles.

title: Tesla FSD 14 ‘Feels Sentient,’ Second Biggest Update Ever: Musk
content: Elon Musk has announced that Tesla's upcoming Full Self-Driving (FSD) update, version 14, will be the second biggest update to the system after version 12. Musk claims that FSD 14 'feels alive' and will feature a model with 10 times more parameters than the current version, resulting in a 'dramatic gain' in performance. The update will also reduce the frequency of driver monitoring alerts, 'nagging' users less. FSD 14 is currently in the training and testing phase, with a potential public release in late September. According to Musk, the update will be a significant improvement over the current version, making self-driving feel more natural and human-like. As Tesla prepares to launch its Robotaxi service to the public, FSD 14 is shaping up to be one of the most ambitious updates to the autonomous driving system yet.
